# Simple maze: Soar agent from the Rosie teaching script

**Runnable.** `simple-maze.soar` loads the shared library (`Soar/soar-library`, v2.42) and `simple-maze-rules.soar` (11 task rules, generated by `gen.py` from the statements in `english-input.txt`; `tools/rosie_grid.py`). Generated 18 Nov 2026. Needs Soar 9.6.6 (or the PyPI soar-sml bindings).

## Run

    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . simple-maze.soar --seed 1 --cap 60000
    python3 ../../tools/run_agent.py . simple-maze.soar --json | python3 ../../tools/check_moves.py simple-maze init-mazerc.world

`python3 gen.py WORLD` writes the same rules with another example state as the initial world.

## Results (library v2.42, 18 Nov 2026)

Example states (`gen.py WORLD`, `run_agent.py --check`): init-mazerc: goal false, failure false; final-mazerc: goal true, failure false.

Seeds 1-3, cap 60,000 decisions; plans replayed independently by `check_moves.py` (legality from the action statements, the losing conditions, the goal).

| Seed | Outcome | Decisions | Actions | Replay |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | success | 170 | 3 | goal holds |
| 2 | success | 129 | 3 | goal holds |
| 3 | success | 162 | 3 | goal holds |

## Translation

- Operator block-step (argument1 = the blue block, argument2 = the clear location), statement 5; adjacent (statement 7)
  is a static relation between locations (A-G1); clear is a maintained one-argument relation (statement 6). The black
  blocks are walls only in that they stand on locations, which are then not clear.
- The goal: a blue block is on a blue location.
Propose initialize-simple-maze when its conditions below hold.

The assumption codes (A-S, A-G, A-C, A-P) are explained in `tools/rosie_grid.py` and `../../PILOT.md`.
